analysis.title: U.S. Economic & Interest Rate Outlook: Critical Paths (November 2026)
key_insights: Northern Trust's base case remains continued U.S. growth despite policy uncertainty, Middle East tension and bond market repricing. It says it is too soon to say the worst is over.

October payrolls rose 165,000, above expectations, with upward revisions to prior months. Professional sector hiring returned and wage growth of 3.1% suggests the long downtrend in wage gains is flattening.

October CPI rose 0.4% MoM and 0.3% core. No October 2025 price data exists due to last year's shutdown, so no YoY rate was published, though it would have been near 4%. Durable goods price increases suggest tariff pass-through continues.

Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualized, led by business investment in data centers. Nonresidential fixed investment rose 12.7%, the strongest since 2011, but import-heavy computing hardware widened the trade deficit.
Northern Trust expects the FOMC to hike in December and again in Q1. If hikes end at three, they reverse the 2025 easing.

The 10-year Treasury yield has settled below its recent 5.3% peak. Absent new inflation shocks yields should hold, with indebtedness, sticky inflation and Fed tightening limiting how far rates can fall.
30-year mortgage rates are well over 7% and existing home sales fell to a 16-year low in October, leaving housing stalled.

Midterm results showed popular pushback against AI data center development in referenda. Northern Trust expects local policy to slow some future projects but not halt those underway, so AI investment remains a growth source.
Middle East: both sides signaled willingness to escalate and openness to a ceasefire. Falling energy prices reflect market optimism.

Middle East escalation could reverse declining energy prices.
Bond market repricing drivers are not durably settled.

geopolitical: Middle East: official statements from both sides indicate willingness to escalate and openness to a ceasefire, and declining energy prices reflect market optimism.
U.S. midterm elections reduced some funding risks but do not change the administration's executive-led policy priorities.
Tariffs are still working through durable goods prices.

tension_points.bull_case: Data centers drove a 12.7% rise in nonresidential fixed investment and Northern Trust expects AI investment to remain a source of growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Midterm referenda showed widespread opposition to data center development, and import-heavy hardware widened the trade deficit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Local policy changes that halt projects underway rather than only slowing future development.
